title: Site Health
description: Runs WordPress's direct + async Site Health checks and exposes the Info / debug-data report.

documentation.purpose: A two-tab Site Health surface. The Status tab runs the synchronous DIRECT tests server-side (via the workspace `GET /wp-admin-workspaces/v1/site-health/tests` endpoint, which wraps `WP_Site_Health::get_tests()['direct']`) and the ASYNC tests in parallel against core's per-id `/wp-site-health/v1/tests/{id}` routes; the async test list is enumerated dynamically from the same workspace endpoint's `async` registry (honoring the `site_status_tests` filter, so plugin tests flow through) instead of being hardcoded. The Info tab renders an accordion over `WP_Debug_Data::debug_data()` (via `GET /wp-admin-workspaces/v1/site-health/info`) with a Copy button that OMITS fields flagged `private`. Each test card shows status (Good / Recommended / Critical) and a trusted HTML description; the count line spans direct + async. The authorization-header test is probed with an `Authorization: Basic` header (mirroring classic) so the server can observe whether it strips the header. `iframe:site-health.php` remains the full-fidelity fallback.

reads.purpose: Workspace endpoint: returns `direct` (synchronously-run direct-test results) + `async` (the async-test registry: id / label / has_rest) so the app can run direct tests and enumerate async tests without a hardcoded list.
One request per async test id (from the dynamic registry); runs `Promise.all`. Each returns `{ status, label, description }`.
Workspace endpoint: returns `WP_Debug_Data::debug_data()` as `sections[]` with each field's `private` flag preserved. Drives the Info tab accordion + the private-omitting copy payload.

states.renders: Toolbar Re-run button shows loading; cards without results show Spinner.
Cards already-completed show their status pill; remaining cards show Spinner.
All cards show status + description; toolbar shows category counts.
Error text below the toolbar (plus per-test error captured in results).

states.when: Info tab selected && sections is an array
states.renders: Copy button + an accordion of debug-data sections (Collapsible); each field row shows label + value, private fields carry a 'Private' badge.

That test's card shows status=recommended with an "A test is unavailable" label and a friendly description naming the test — matching classic's soft "unavailable" notice rather than a critical failure that would skew the score.

interactions.effect: `runTests()` fires automatically — fetches direct results + async registry, then runs async tests in parallel.
Fetches `/site-health/info` and renders the debug-data accordion.
Bumps a run token; the active tab re-runs (Status) or re-fetches (Info).

Writes a plain-text report to the clipboard via `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, OMITTING private fields; success/error snackbar. Falls back to an error snackbar when the clipboard API is unavailable.

a11y.focus-management: Native focus order — toolbar button + card content.
a11y.screen-reader: Per-test status surfaces as a Badge with intent (`success` / `warning` / `error` / `neutral`). The badge text is the live status; no aria-live region announces completion.

constraints.note: Test descriptions arrive as HTML from `/wp-site-health/v1/tests/{id}`. WordPress core authors these strings; we render via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. ESLint disable comment in source notes the trust boundary.

Each test's request is wrapped in try/catch so one failing test doesn't reject the `Promise.all`. Failed tests show as recommended ("A test is unavailable") rather than critical — matching classic, so a transient network blip doesn't read as a critical failure. Preserves partial results.

The async-test list is enumerated from the workspace `/site-health/tests` endpoint's `async` registry, which is built from `WP_Site_Health::get_tests()` (post `site_status_tests` filter), so plugin-contributed tests appear. A static `FALLBACK_ASYNC_TESTS` list is used only if that endpoint is unreachable.

The Info-tab copy payload skips any field flagged `private` (matching core's clipboard format). Private fields are still DISPLAYED in the accordion with a 'Private' badge — only the copy export omits them.
`navigator.clipboard.writeText` can be absent (insecure context) or reject; guarded with an explicit availability check + an error snackbar, mirroring MediaDetails.
